sql.description: This line pastes {subject} into a database question. The database can treat {subject} as part of the command instead of as one value.
sql.effect: a person who can change {subject} can change what the database is asked to do
sql.remediation: Take {subject} out of the question text. Keep the question as fixed words and pass {subject} as a separate argument. The line to rewrite is `{line}`.

secret.description: This line writes a secret value into {subject}. Anyone who can read the file can read that secret.
secret.effect: the secret in {subject} can be read from the file
secret.remediation: Delete the secret value from {subject}. Read {subject} from the secret store when the program runs, and leave no secret in the file.

action.description: This line runs {subject} from a tag. A tag can be moved, so the workflow can run different code than the copy that was reviewed.
action.effect: the workflow can run a different copy of {subject} than the one that was reviewed
action.remediation: Replace the tag on {subject} with the 40-character commit for that release, and keep the version in a comment.

exec.description: This line runs {subject} as a command. The person who supplies that text chooses what runs.
exec.effect: the call runs whatever text is in {subject}
exec.remediation: Delete the call that runs {subject}. Keep {subject} as data for one operation written in full in this file. The line to change is `{line}`.

deser.description: This line rebuilds objects from {subject}. The loader can construct more than the data fields this file expects.
deser.effect: the loader can build objects from {subject} while it reads the value
deser.remediation: Stop passing {subject} to the loader. Read a data format that cannot construct objects. The line to change is `{line}`.

ssrf.description: This line sends a request to an address taken from {subject}. The program does not write the one host it is allowed to call.
ssrf.effect: the request can go to whatever host is in {subject}
ssrf.remediation: Write the allowed host in the file and stop passing {subject} as the address. The line to change is `{line}`.

xss.description: This line writes {subject} into the page as HTML. A caller can change how the page is built.
xss.effect: the page includes whatever is in {subject} as markup
xss.remediation: Put {subject} in a text node, not in HTML. The line to change is `{line}`.

auth.description: This line opens {subject} without naming who is allowed to call it.
auth.effect: a caller this file does not name can use {subject}
auth.remediation: Require a role, an owner, and a state check before {subject} runs, or delete {subject} if the application does not need it.

wildcard.description: This line grants a wildcard. The permission is not limited to one action and one resource.
wildcard.effect: the policy allows more than the operations this workload performs
wildcard.remediation: Replace the wildcard in `{line}` with the named principal, actions, and resources this workload uses.

tls.description: This line turns off the check that confirms the other computer's certificate.
tls.effect: the program will talk to a computer it did not verify
tls.remediation: Delete the setting in `{line}` that turns certificate checks off.

debug.description: This line leaves the debug switch on. The running program can show internals to a caller.
debug.effect: debug output stays available where this program runs

path.description: This line builds a file path from {subject}. The path can leave the directory this file should use.
path.effect: the program can open a file chosen by {subject}
path.remediation: Delete {subject} from the file path. Open a file whose path is written in full in this file. The line to change is `{line}`.

archive.description: This line extracts an archive without limiting the path of each entry.
archive.effect: an entry in the archive can write outside the directory this file expects
archive.remediation: Delete extractall from `{line}`. Extract only names that stay inside one directory written in this file.

jwt.description: This line accepts a token without checking its signature.
jwt.effect: a token this file did not verify can be accepted
jwt.remediation: Delete verify=False or the none algorithm from `{line}`. Accept one named algorithm and check the signature.
